source.quote: Eversolo's own specification table for the DMP-A8, read 2026-11-24. DAC: « AK4191EQ + AK4499EX ». DAC Decoding: « Supports up to stereo DSD512 Native and PCM 768kHz 32-bit. » USB-B Audio Input: « USB Compatibility: Windows (10,11), Mac, Android, iOS. Supports up to stereo DSD512 and PCM 768kHz 32-bit. » Optical/Coaxial Input: « Supports up to stereo PCM 192kHz 24-bit and DSD64 DoP. » ARC Input: « Supports up to stereo PCM 192kHz 24-bit. »

facts.chip: Two AKM parts named by the maker's own table as « AK4191EQ + AK4499EX »: the AK4191 is the modulator and the AK4499EX the converter. The same pairing as gustard/a26, and the reason a chip model needs a ROLE per part - a modulator's order is a property of the modulator, not of a vendor.

_firsts: FIRST RECORD OF THE POPULATION PASS, and it is the template. Seven things in this catalogue are exercised here for the first time: kind network_player; a source.kind that is not `import` (datasheet, the maker's own published specification); source_names_subject, which CONTRIBUTING has asked for from the start and no claim had ever set; inputs.bits, inputs.dop_possible and inputs.native_dsd_possible, three fields registered as planned and carried by nobody; and the hdmi interface, defined and never used. A read_on that is the day THIS page was read, not a batch date shared by 43 other claims.
_what_is_not_asserted: The page does not say whether USB carries DoP as well as native DSD, so inputs.usb.dop_possible is ABSENT rather than false - nobody filled it in, which is not the same as a no. No level-3 field is claimed: the maker publishes what the device accepts and says nothing about what it does with it, which is this catalogue's whole premise.
